BIBLIOTECA — CATALOGUE RESEARCH, 17 OCTOBER 2026

Private website: https://biblioteca-family-atlas.lfernandez85.chatgpt.site/research.html

Scope: every one of the 49,780 catalogue records was screened. These include books, papers, continuations and cross-references, not a count of distinct physical books.

Author-name entries: 22,785
Public biographical descriptions / proposed identities: 11,099
Default author reference images: 4,544
Alternative identity candidates retained: 42,567
Public authority people compared: 369,132
Additional OCR attribution links: 5,090
Previously unattributed records recovered by heading review: 3,623
Unattributed records remaining: 7,777

Possible book matches: 2,582
Public bibliographic records compared: 768,442
Book records with reference images: 2,585
Book records with multiple reference images: 286
Edition-specific survival investigations: 23
Records with a documented numerical lower bound: 22

Confidence is displayed separately for identity/attribution, biography or metadata, images, and survival evidence. High/medium/low are ordinal research assessments, not statistical probabilities. False matches are expected among tentative candidates. All original scans and OCR remain linked.

Every final author-name entry was compared against the retrieved authority subset; this is not an exhaustive search of all public authorities. Candidate identities can be namesakes. A chooser retains alternatives. Names and spelling variants have not been merged into a verified person census.

All book records were compared against a large, selected scientific/historical metadata corpus. Source catalogue notes and subjects are labeled as such; they are not substitutes for independently researched content summaries. Image matches can be other editions or tentative work matches and do not depict the family's actual copy. Remote image availability can change.

Surviving copies: the strongest new findings are Gilbert 1628 (86 known copies in a published census), Agricola Paris 1533 (at least 56 reported copies), and Pliny 1499 (at least 11 documented copies). Bounds remain open where a finite worldwide estimate cannot be supported. Newton's 1714 edition has a conditional range of 4 to approximately 750 based on known holdings and an estimated original print run; this is not a likely surviving range. All qualifications and source links are on the book pages.

Validation passed for record IDs, author/book links, PDF paths, field-level confidence, image provenance, counts, survival evidence, and JavaScript syntax. Browser checks covered candidate switching, confidence filtering, profile loading, and image-gallery selection. Sources were sampled and strongest leads deepened; every attribution was not manually verified.

OFFLINE / LOCAL USE
The biblioteca folder contains the webpage and original catalogue PDFs. Run a local web server from that folder (for example: python3 -m http.server 8765) and open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ . Browser fetch restrictions mean double-clicking index.html is insufficient. External images and source links require internet access; catalogue scans and locally saved reference images are included.

Entry points: index.html, authors.html, books.html, catalogue.html, research.html.
Data: authors-data.json (compact index), author-profiles/*.json.gz (full profiles and alternatives), author-records/*.json.gz, books-data.json, book-records/*.json.gz, research-data.json, unattributed-records.json.gz.

Large profile data files are gzip-compressed; the website opens them automatically in current browsers. The local output folder also retains full JSON copies.
